record.original_question: Find the smallest $p>0$ such that we can solve an $n x n$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(T_A*bar kappa_p)$ arithmetic operations, where $bar kappa_p$ is the $p$-averaged condition number of the singular values of $A$, whereas $T_A$ is either $n^2$ or $nnz(A)$.

evidence.quote: Find the smallest $p>0$ such that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $\tilde O(\mathcal{T}_A\cdot\bar\kappa_p)$ arithmetic operations, where $\bar\kappa_p$ is the $p$-averaged condition number of the singular values of $A$, whereas $\mathcal{T}_A$ is either $n^2$ or $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be an invertible matrix with singular values $\sigma_1(A) \ge \sigma_2(A) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_n(A) > 0$, and for $p > 0$ define the $p$-averaged condition number
$$\bar{\kappa}_p(A) \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{\sigma_1(A)}{\sigma_i(A)}\right)^p\right)^{1/p}.$$
Let $\mathcal{T}_A$ denote either $n^2$ or $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ (the number of nonzero entries of $A$). We say a randomized algorithm solves the linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy if, for any input vector $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and any target accuracy $\varepsilon > 0$, it returns (with high probability) a vector $\tilde{x}$ with $\|\tilde{x} - A^{-1}b\| \le \varepsilon \|A^{-1}b\|$, with running time depending only polylogarithmically on $1/\varepsilon$.

Determine the smallest real number $p > 0$ such that there exists an algorithm solving every such linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy using $\widetilde{O}\big(\mathcal{T}_A \cdot \bar{\kappa}_p(A)\big)$ arithmetic operations (where $\widetilde{O}$ hides factors polylogarithmic in $n$, $\bar\kappa_p(A)$, and $1/\varepsilon$).
artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence was found that this question (smallest $p$ for which $\widetilde{O}(\mathcal{T}_A \bar\kappa_p)$-time high-accuracy linear solvers exist) has been resolved. General results on averaged condition numbers exist, but a tight characterization of the optimal $p$ does not appear in the readily searchable literature, so the status is unknown.

status_evidence.title: Average condition number for solving linear equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies an average condition number and average loss of precision for solving linear equations, comparing average case to worst case.
status_evidence.claim: Averaged condition numbers have been studied for linear system solving, but no tight result on the optimal p for O(T_A · κ̄_p) running time is reported.

status_evidence.title: Condition: The Geometry of Numerical Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Running time of iterative numerical algorithms can be bounded in terms of input size and a condition number μ(x).
status_evidence.claim: Iterative solver complexity is commonly expressed via condition numbers; the precise optimal averaging exponent p remains a research question.
